title: Take a shot every time I say “Ballroom culture”💀 #Cats #BallroomCats ...
transcript: I am a certified cats the musical hater, and last night I saw cats the Gelical Ball. This is a complete reimagining of cats that blends the musical cats with the world of ballroom culture. And honestly, despite my feelings about this show, that premise alone was enough to get me excited, and I knew I had to be their first preview. Now here I am in the year of our Lord 2024 to tell you that a production of cats is actually good. I think that this production not only completely delivers on its premise, but is everything you wanted to be and more. Even as someone who is not super familiar with ballroom culture, it was really clear to me how much effort went in to make it not just feel authentic, but to honor the culture and history of ballroom. Several of the performers formers in the show are icons of the ballroom scene, including temptress, who plays Grisabella, and Junior Labiga, who plays old Gus, who is most well known as the MC for the Paris is Burning Ball, which was featured in the documentary of the same name. I actually highly recommend checking out that documentary if you wanna learn more about ballroom culture. And I do actually think it is helpful to come into this production with at least some knowledge of ballroom culture. Like I said, I don't know a ton about ballroom culture. Most of what I know comes from the Netflix Series pose, which I've been told is pretty accurate. But I did think just knowing the basics of, like, how the houses work, how the competitions work, uh, was really helpful in kind of grounding my understanding of what was happening on stage. I don't think that you will be lost if you don't understand ballroom. It's pretty straightforward. But I do think it will enhance your experience. I also have to shout out the costumes by Queen Jean, because they are spectacular. They are colorful, they are bold, and Andre the Shields is wearing one of the craziest wigs I've ever seen. I, like, audibly gasped when it came on stage. A lot of the costumes do have subtle knots to cats, like animal print or just, like, fur accents, but for the most part, they are just like street clothes or fashion. I was just so thoroughly entertained the entire time. It feels like a love letter to both cats and ballroom. And even if you hate cats like me, I do think you should see the show because it just might change your mind.
reasoning: The reviewer is a self-proclaimed 'cats hater' who was completely won over by this production, calling it 'actually good' and saying it 'might change your mind.' Strong enthusiasm throughout with specific praise for authenticity, costumes, and entertainment value.
